clue.text: Ripped into eight or nine pieces

indicators.note: the answer lies in pieces of the run eight or nine, spread across the end and start of its words

explanation.surface: Something has been torn up into eight or nine scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' signals that the answer is lifted from the joined letters of 'eight or nine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something ripped has been pulled apart.

clue.text: One bringing up children behind the Queen

parts.note: the behind is the backside or rear
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A parent or nanny stands behind the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises children is a raiser of them, the noun from the verb meaning to raise young.

clue.text: Griffin she turned into food

indicators.note: turned, as in transformed, tells us to rearrange the letters of Griffin she

explanation.surface: A mythical griffin is magically transformed into something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded cod sticks are a staple British children's meal, an example of food.

clue.text: Like Jack in The Shining: extremely scary — chop, chop!

indicators.note: the first chop is an instruction to cut up and rearrange the letters that follow
extremely picks the outermost letters of the word scary

explanation.surface: A film buff describes the axe-wielding Jack Torrance, scary as he hacks through a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely scary' gives SY; 'chop' then rearranges SY with the second CHOP. 'chop, chop' reads as 'hurry up' but is indicator plus fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Torrance in Kubrick's horror film goes murderously mad, so he is a deranged killer type.

clue.text: Fuel container Tom can't use, but ___?

definitions.meaning: a flat-sided metal can for carrying petrol
in the Tom and Jerry cartoons the mouse always gets the better of the cat, so the blank is filled by the mouse's name plus can

explanation.definitionFit: The flat steel petrol can takes its name from the German soldiers who designed it; the cartoon mouse shares the nickname.

clue.text: Vehicle that carries regular team and another

indicators.note: regular takes every other letter of the word team

parts.note: another team: a side of eleven players is written XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A minibus ferries one sports team and then a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another team, an XI, as cricket and football elevens are written.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a hired car, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Spoil bag, so tea's stewed

indicators.note: stewed tea has been left too long, and the word here tells us to rearrange the letters of bag, so tea

explanation.surface: A tea bag left in too long ruins the brew.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after tea stands for 'is', a link before the indicator 'stewed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck something deliberately is to spoil it; the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Men's back exercise — skipping, say?

indicators.note: back tells us to read the letters for men from the end

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers, i.e. men
PE is physical education, exercise at school

explanation.surface: Soldiers do a back workout, perhaps by jumping a cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord used for jumping exercise is the object behind skipping; the question mark flags this example-style definition.

clue.text: Money problem for the shoe-dwelling old woman?

definitions.text: Money problem for the shoe-dwelling old woman?

parts.words: Money problem for the shoe-dwelling old woman?
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the old woman who lived in a shoe had so many children she did not know what to do: too much offspring, and issue also means printing too much money

explanation.surface: The nursery-rhyme woman in the shoe has financial troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing more currency than allowed is a monetary failing; issue also means offspring, which she had in excess.

clue.text: Siege in the style of Farah?

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of
Mo Farah, the British Olympic distance runner

explanation.surface: A long-drawn-out contest run like one of Mo Farah's races.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Farah is a British long-distance champion runner.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1836 Texan mission besieged by Mexican forces is a famous example of a siege.

clue.text: Bearing of player in the Iran-Contra affair

definitions.meaning: Oliver, the US Marine officer at the centre of the 1980s arms-for-hostages scandal

explanation.surface: Someone describes the role of a figure in the Reagan-era arms scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point is a bearing; Lt Col Oliver of that surname ran the secret arms deals.

clue.text: Tip of rhubarb? No, I crave tripe!

definitions.text: Tip of rhubarb? No, I crave tripe!

indicators.note: tripe is rubbish or nonsense, so the letters before it are rearranged into a new order
the tip of a word is its first letter, here of rhubarb

explanation.surface: Offered a stick of rhubarb, someone refuses and demands offal instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip of rhubarb' gives R, which joins NOICRAVE for 'tripe' to rearrange. The whole clue is also what a meat-eater might say.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat-eater turns down vegetables and wants animal flesh such as tripe: the whole clue describes one.

clue.text: Green Goblin initially breaks into Number 10 — Spider-man's unaffected by this

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

indicators.note: breaks into means one piece forces its way inside another

parts.note: the figures 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of Goblin

explanation.surface: Spider-Man's foe the Green Goblin raids Downing Street, while the web-slinger keeps his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 is the Prime Minister's house, but here it is IO, the digits read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear of heights brings dizziness, which a wall-climbing superhero clearly never suffers.

clue.text: Maybe I swear to overthrow the French

parts.note: to swear is to vow or promise

indicators.note: to overthrow is to turn upside down, so in a down clue the French article is read backwards

parts.note: le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Someone vows to topple the French government.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter I is one of the five letters a, e, i, o, u, so it exemplifies the group.

clue.text: Uri can't bend screen

indicators.note: bend tells us to twist the letters of Uri can't into a new shape

explanation.surface: Uri Geller, the spoon-bender, fails to bend a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Uri Geller was a TV performer famous for bending spoons.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape hung across a window or stage serves as a screen.

clue.text: Officials arrest girls misbehaving without latitude

indicators.note: misbehaving suggests disorder, so the letters of arrest girls are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for latitude on maps

explanation.surface: Officials detain some unruly girls who have been given too much freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes L, latitude, out of ARRESTGIRLS before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorders of births, deaths and marriages are public officials.

clue.text: Bottom of messy drain

indicators.note: messy describes letters in disarray, so the word drain is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone peers into the bottom of a clogged drain.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything is its bottom; the word is a synonym.

clue.text: Grown out of Nick Park's 1993 trousers?

indicators.note: letters out of place are disordered, so the word Grown is rearranged

explanation.surface: Wallace has outgrown his trousers from the 1993 animated film.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Park's 1993 Wallace and Gromit film is titled after a pair of techno-trousers; the question mark marks the definition-by-example.
explanation.definitionFit: In the film title the trousers are described as incorrect, so the adjective fills the gap.

clue.text: Take for a ride via trams?

parts.note: read the answer as two words: put the letters of smart out of order and you get trams

explanation.surface: Taking someone for a ride on public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, split as an instruction, scrambles SMART to give 'trams'.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone for a ride is an idiom meaning to trick or outwit them.

clue.text: Crew finally returns from Vietnam

indicators.note: returns means the letters go back the other way
finally takes the closing part of the word Vietnam, which is also the slang short form of it

explanation.surface: A unit of soldiers comes home from the war in Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nam is the slang term for Vietnam and also its final three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To crew a ship is to staff it, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Mmmm … I'm upset by large cats

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the letters of I'm are read upward

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
lions are big cats

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs in alarm as huge cats approach.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the Roman thousand, so MM is a thousand thousand; Mmmm is two lots of that.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman numerals M is a thousand; M times M is a thousand thousand, and two such make the plural.

clue.text: Country ignoring church, starting to descend into sin

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the letters for church from the country

parts.note: Greece is the country
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: starting to takes the first letter of descend

explanation.surface: A godless nation begins its slide into wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is one of the seven deadly sins, so it is an example of sin.

clue.text: In the future city goes left, then sideways

parts.note: later means in the future

indicators.note: in an across clue going left means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A city's road plan veers left, then sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to the side, as in a sideways move or thinking, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Stop fighting when armistice really starts

definitions.text: Stop fighting when armistice really starts

indicators.note: fighting suggests a scuffle, so the letters of Stop are jumbled
starts takes the first letter of when, armistice and really

explanation.surface: The war ends; peace truly begins once the armistice is signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' rearranged by 'fighting' gives POST; 'starts' gives W, A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The period after hostilities cease and peace begins is the time the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Small European bird spotted in outskirts of Prague

indicators.note: something spotted in a place is found within it, so the pieces go inside
outskirts are the outside edges, the first and last letters of Prague

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a small European songbird on the edge of Prague.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, this adjective means small and dainty, often of a woman's build.

clue.text: Dowager welcomes knight's opening

indicators.note: welcomes means taking a guest in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dowager is a widow holding her late husband's title
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A titled widow lets in a knight for a social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after knight stands for 'is', a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazed gap in a wall is an opening; the noun also means an opportunity.

clue.text: Trouble in bed? Politician's nail breaks

indicators.note: in places the following pieces inside the word for a bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: breaks tells us the letters of nail fall apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bedridden, a politician also has a broken fingernail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble in bed' reads as a bedroom problem, but 'in' is the container signal; 'breaks' gives LAIN. A complaint is also a medical ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or ailment is a trouble; the noun often means a medical condition.

clue.text: Young English 8?

parts.note: a cub is a young animal such as a fox or bear

explanation.surface: A young English person aged eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Two multiplied by itself three times gives 8, so 8 is an example of a third power.

clue.text: Craving for flour — is it regular?

indicators.note: regular takes the second and fourth letters of flour and of is it

explanation.surface: A baker's craving for flour raises the question of whether it is normal.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong desire or longing is a synonym for craving.

clue.text: Continue with German sausage roll? Not I

indicators.note: Not drops the letter I from the sausage
roll means the letters turn over, read backwards

parts.note: a wiener is a frankfurter-style German sausage

explanation.surface: A diner asks for more: a German sausage in a bun, but not for them.
explanation.walkthrough: WIENER reversed by 'roll' is RENEIW; 'Not I' removes I.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on with a lease or subscription is to extend it again, so continue fits.

clue.text: Direction to the Guardian's street

parts.note: the Guardian, as the newspaper, speaks of itself as we

explanation.surface: Directions to the newspaper's street.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter publishes in the Guardian, so the paper is 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point, the way the sun sets, is a direction.

clue.text: Offers to capture rebel leader and those taking flight

indicators.note: to capture means to hold inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: bids are offers at an auction

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of rebel

explanation.surface: A bounty is offered for the rebel chief and those fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Feathered creatures fly, so those taking flight describes them, playing on fleeing.

clue.text: Infamous doughnuts, with holes on the outside, eaten in North America

indicators.note: eaten in means swallowed inside, so the pieces go within N and US

parts.note: US is the United States

indicators.note: on the outside places two holes either side of the doughnuts

parts.note: O looks like a hole, so two holes are two Os
tori, the plural of torus, are doughnut-shaped solids in geometry

explanation.surface: Holey doughnuts eaten in North America are a byword for bad health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doughnuts' is TORI, the geometric shape; 'holes' are Os put outside it to give OTORIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous for something bad is infamous; the two are synonyms.
